project.heading: Finsight, a project I keep tabs on
project.body: Young fish die early at a high rate, and you can see trouble coming in how they behave. Finsight is my idea for using pattern recognition on video, through computer vision, to catch early signs of disease, stress, hunger or low oxygen before it spreads. It started with my brother's farm in mind, and I still keep tabs on it.

about.title: About Roanin Podkin
about.description: Who Roanin Podkin is: Vacaville, a fish farm in Washington, UCSB economics and a semester in Madrid, two months solo in Asia, teaching himself AI, La Cumbre, and now Avoca in Santa Barbara.

sections.heading: Where I started
paragraphs: I grew up in Vacaville, California. I've played golf since I was a kid, made Eagle Scout, and worked my first job at In-N-Out for a year in high school. I was always looking for a way to make a few dollars. The work ethic was there from the start; the jobs just gave it somewhere to go.

My older brother Colby runs a fish farm in Washington, and he was the first entrepreneur I watched up close. We strategized together through high school and college, and I spent a couple of summers working with him. Being around the fish gave me Finsight, an idea for catching early signs of disease, stress, hunger or low oxygen from how fish behave on video. I still keep tabs on it.

sections.heading: Santa Barbara
paragraphs: I studied economics at UC Santa Barbara, class of 2026, with a semester in Madrid in fall 2024 that I used to see as much of Europe as I could.

At the start of my sophomore year I took a job at La Cumbre Country Club to meet the members and play free golf. The members, successful business owners, became mentors. We golfed together and they talked to me about my career and my life. It's through them that I found Avoca.

sections.heading: Stepping back
paragraphs: The summer before my last year I went to Asia alone for almost two months: Taiwan, Japan, Vietnam, Thailand, Singapore and Indonesia. I got PADI-certified on Ko Tao and spent four days on a boat from Lombok to Flores, with whale sharks in between. Mostly it was a chance to step back and ask whether I liked who I'd become and who I wanted to be. I still do that audit on purpose.

sections.heading: Then AI happened
paragraphs: I came back in the middle of the AI boom and went deep: hours of videos a day, then testing what the models could actually do, building agents, automating the boring work. I started telling people, then doing it for them, and got a business license as an AI consultant. The biggest project was La Cumbre, where I presented to the whole team and then completed a contract. The most useful thing I did was sit down with owners one-on-one and teach them.
My mentors said get real industry experience. I look for good leaders, and I found them at Avoca, where I joined the sales development team in Santa Barbara in July 2026.

sections.heading: Off the clock
paragraphs: Hikes, new countries, side quests, golf, pickup soccer, the gym, runs. Mostly anything active with people I like.

values.heading: How I decide
values.intro: I keep my values written out. Relationships come first. The rest matter just as much as each other.

first.name: Relationships
first.line: People come first. I care about doing right by them, and I'm happiest doing things with other people.

rest.name: Freedom
rest.line: To say what I want and do what I want, when I want.

rest.name: Resilience
rest.line: To push through whenever it's needed.

values.rule: Every opportunity I assess, I check against my values and my big goals, and make sure it's aligned with both.
values.wallNote: There's a note on my wall that says retire by 30. Underneath it: true retirement is when you stop sacrificing today for tomorrow.
